messages:
sam_support: FYI incoming customer escalation (acct: acme-inc). They're seeing a mix of 429s and sudden latency spikes when using model rwd-large-v2-64k with ~40k context. Started ~11:23 UTC. Sample req IDs: req-9ab3, req-9ab4. Customer also reports intermittent 401s during retries. Any quick pointers? :exclamation:

ops_bot: [Alert] rate-limit breach on model rwd-large-v2-64k — 95th RPM=78, TPM_tokens=1.2M, thresholds: RPM=60, TPM=1,000,000. Incident RL-1951.

alex_chen: I'll pull per-model metrics + token breakdown. @jordan_sre can you grab the logs for req-9ab3 / req-9ab4 and capture the full response bodies?

jordan_sre: On it. quick note — we count TPM as consumed+generated tokens; very long contexts (~40k tokens) push TPM up fast even at modest request rates. I repro'd locally; commands below.

jordan_sre: ```bash
# quick repro (truncated context)
curl -i -X POST "https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate" \\
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDACTED" \\
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \\
  -d '{"model":"rwd-large-v2-64k","input":"<40k tokens of context...>","max_tokens":512}'
```

jordan_sre: sample response we saw when limit hit:
```http
HTTP/1.1 429 Too Many Requests
{
  "error": "rate_limit_exceeded",
  "message": "per-model TPM or RPM exceeded",
  "quota": {"model":"rwd-large-v2-64k","rpm":60,"tpm":1000000}
}
```

kim_w: Looks like TPM is the primary bottleneck here, not raw RPM. The intermittent 401s could be from the client's library timing out / retrying while our auth/billing checks are under stress — can cause cascading failures.

alex_chen: Confirmed in metrics: TPM peaked ~1.18M and RPM ~65 during the window. We do enforce both per-model RPM and TPM. For long-context workloads TPM will often be the limiter. See internal doc: https://redwood.ai/docs/limits (shared).

sam_support: Customer asked for immediate mitigations. Suggested short-term options: 1) reduce context length or do prefix trimming, 2) enable local prefix/KV caching, 3) lower concurrency (limit parallel clients to ~4), 4) implement exponential backoff with jitter, 5) switch to rwd-compact-32k or lower-context model, or 6) request a Dedicated/reserved capacity eval. They want repro steps to show it's quota-related.

jordan_sre: I also ran a simple python loop to demonstrate TPM burn: 
```python
import requests
for i in range(120):
  requests.post(url, headers=auth, json=payload_with_40k)
```
After ~30 iterations TPM crosses 1M and 429s start.

alex_chen: If they want a quota increase we need: expected sustained RPM/TPM, burst profile, and business justification. Created ticket RWD-2345 for uplift request and escalation to eng-dedicated.

ops_bot: ops_bot: ticket RWD-2345 linked to alert RL-1951. Notifying eng-oncall.

kim_w: Also check billing/account status on their API key. Under load, auth/billing subsystem retries can surface as 401/402 to clients. Recommend customer confirm billing is active and not hitting any per-account rate guard. We can do a temporary per-customer quota bump if contract allows.

sam_support: I'll send the customer the minimal curl + python repro and ask them to try with reduced context first. Asking them to provide a sanitized payload (no PII) for us to repro on their account if needed.

jordan_sre: I'll monitor the model TPM/RPM for the next 60m and add a transient early-throttle rule for >30k contexts if TPM > 900k to avoid auth/backoff cascades.

alex_chen: Follow-ups: 1) Add a support KB note clarifying TPM = token-weighted minute limit for per-model quotas; 2) Product: consider per-project token budgets or predictive throttling on long-context profiles; 3) Ops: evaluate faster early-reject for very large contexts when near TPM.

sam_support: Thanks everyone — I'll update RWD-2345 and provide the customer an ETA of 24hrs for next steps. :white_check_mark:
